sources.title: Structured Hello interview source containing the longest-palindrome prompt

claims.text: The source asks for the longest palindromic substring with space-complexity optimization without specifying language, null/empty behavior, tie-breaking, or Unicode comparison units.
Enumerating odd and even centers and expanding while the two boundary units match finds every candidate palindrome while storing only constant-size search state.

The exact candidate has O(n^2) worst-case time and O(1) peak auxiliary search state, uses Java UTF-16 char units, rejects null, returns empty for empty input, and resolves equal-length maxima by earliest start.

validation.command: extract the exact candidate Java block, compile it inside an independent harness, and compare deterministic/exhaustive/randomized outputs against a brute-force longest-palindrome oracle
validation.reported_stdout: PASS exact_candidate null=rejected deterministic=15 exhaustive=3280 randomized=20000 oracle=bruteforce tie=earliest-start odd_even=covered
checks: exact candidate Java implementation compiles under Java 21
null is rejected and empty/single-character inputs follow the explicit contract
15 deterministic cases cover odd/even centers, ties, all-equal strings and boundaries
all 3280 strings of length 0..7 over a three-character alphabet match an independent brute-force oracle
20000 seeded randomized strings of length 0..40 match the independent brute-force oracle
babad resolves to the earliest-start longest palindrome and cbbd exercises the even-center path

findings: The answer preserves the narrow source boundary and clearly labels Java/null/empty/tie/Unicode behavior as implementation contracts rather than source facts.
The center-expansion invariant is explained for both odd and even centers, including the post-loop [left+1,right-1] boundary.
The exact candidate implementation is complete Java rather than pseudocode and matches an independent brute-force oracle on deterministic, exhaustive, and randomized cases.
The O(n^2) worst-case time and O(1) peak auxiliary search state are stated separately from returned-output storage.
Tie behavior is deterministic and explicitly documented; the candidate does not assume an unstated online-judge acceptance rule.
The UTF-16 char-unit boundary is explicit, and code-point/grapheme semantics are correctly left as a different contract.
Manacher is presented as a time-optimization alternative with O(n) auxiliary arrays rather than being conflated with the requested space optimization.
No fabricated production experience or business metric is claimed.
